title: The Streetlifting MUTANT w/ Steel Cable Tendons (Artem Shirokov)
summary: A lifter-profile episode on Russian streetlifter Artem Shirokov: NH analyses his dip and pull-up technique, his tendon 'shock method' training and unconventional biceps work, and contrasts performance technique with what a bodybuilder should do. He ends on Shirokov's philosophy of obsessive dedication and on learning from people who are different, including his split-macronutrient diet.
claims: Calisthenics athletes get the most aesthetic physiques of any non-bodybuilding athletes, despite not training for hypertrophy
Russia has over 5,000 calisthenics parks, which explains why many calisthenics champions come from Eastern Europe
Shirokov's best dip is 170 kg (375 lb) added at 80 kg bodyweight; his 10-rep dip is 120 kg (275 lb) added
Gifted strong individuals have strength skewed above their size; strength standards are individual, so if you got that strong you'd be far bigger
Streetlifters dip with the torso forward and head down, then snap the head up and torso vertical at the bottom to use leverage and momentum
Bodybuilders shouldn't shift torso angle mid-dip: stay leaned forward for chest, or vertical for triceps
Default bodybuilding dip: lean forward like a floating bottle to recruit more chest and use more load, keeping torso and head angles fairly constant
Streetlifters stop dips at humerus parallel because that's the sport standard; bodybuilders can go deeper as comfort and shoulder mobility allow
Bodybuilders should control the eccentric and add a pause at the bottom of dips; most dip injuries happen at the bottom
Bodybuilders should keep weighted dips around 3-5 or 6-10 reps; they never need true 1RMs
Training for 1RM makes your 1RM high relative to rep strength; bodybuilders train rep strength, so 1RM calculators built on strength athletes don't apply
Start dips from locked elbows to squeeze the triceps, and begin with the negative
Kettlebells are better than plates for loading weighted dips and pull-ups: more compact, less dangling, higher off the floor
For aesthetics, direct tendon training is a waste of time: tendons and bones thicken as muscle grows, and naturals rarely outgrow their tendons
Tendon outpacing is mostly a problem for drug users whose muscle outgrows their connective tissue
Shirokov's 'shock method' puts the body in unstable or explosive disadvantaged positions (band dips, ring holds, salmon ladder) so normal heavy lifts feel easier and tendons are conditioned
When catching dynamic loads, let the joint extend and absorb rather than catching locked, like bending knees when landing a jump
Once neurological adaptation is reached, more technical skill is useless for bodybuilding; technique is the enemy of the bodybuilder
Shirokov's strict pull-up 1RM is about 100 kg (225 lb) added
Bodybuilding pull-ups: start with the negative, keep scapulae engaged, slow eccentric, stay under the bar and don't let arms take over
Be honest with yourself about whether you care about strength or size; NH felt nothing hitting strength PRs and is driven by seeing his body change
Short-range rows where the shoulders stay fixed and only the elbow flexes become a biceps exercise biased toward the proximal (upper) biceps
Curls bias the distal biceps; only doing curls can leave an imbalance that looks like poor peak genetics
Don't drop curls for a single trendy movement; if two things work, do both
Chin-ups train the biceps well but are a back exercise, not enough on their own for biceps, and carry real injury risk when strong
Supinated rows risk biceps strain from overextension
Isolating a muscle always makes it grow, whatever the reason for isolating it; that's why gymnasts and calisthenics athletes have big arms
Preventing tendinitis is more important than healing it; NH learned this through chronic elbow tendinitis
To reach a very high level you need to be a little crazy; sane people don't get far
Ridicule of obsessive lifters as 'gymcels' comes from mediocre men who never committed to anything
Shirokov eats lots of red meat and up to 15 eggs at a time and separates protein, fat and carb meals for digestion; NH doesn't do this but says it may help high-intake eaters
Diet is like religion: there are schools of thought, but your relationship with food and training should end up your own
NH prefers Eastern training methods to Western ones
exercises: torso forward, head down, snap upright at bottom, stop at humerus parallel
lock elbows at top, start with negative, controlled tempo, pause at bottom, consistent lean, depth as mobility allows
more chest recruitment and fewer injuries
Dips on resistance bands / band-restricted elbows
Ring hold with small explosive pulses
arms near-locked, little range of motion
arm engaged at top; let the arm extend to absorb the catch
momentum kick, then elbows forward to get over the bar, no eccentric control
arms in front, shoulders fixed, only elbows move
proximal biceps bias with low injury risk
Shirokov trains neck, rare for calisthenics athletes
